title: Next.js Rendering & Caching: Static, Dynamic, Revalidation & Personal Data
concept: Choose how each Next.js App Router page is rendered and cached: static, incremental or dynamic rendering, server and client components, dynamic routes, hydration, cache keys, time-based and on-demand revalidation, and keeping one user's data out of the cache everyone shares.
description: An intermediate course for developers who ship Next.js App Router apps and have been surprised by what the framework cached. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a course page that still shows last week's syllabus after an admin edit, a dashboard rendered statically with the first visitor's name, a hydration warning that only appears for learners in another time zone, a cache key that lets one learner see another learner's progress - and fixes it by deciding where code runs and what may be cached, for how long and for whom: rendering strategies, server and client components, dynamic routes, hydration, cache layers and keys, stale-while-revalidate, tag revalidation and personal data. 10 lessons with quizzes on real code, headers and logs, and hands-on TypeScript challenges.

lessons.title: Choose static, incremental or dynamic rendering for each page
Server or client component: decide where each piece runs
Dynamic routes: params, prebuilt pages and not-found
Hydration: make the server HTML and the client agree
Map the cache layers and build a safe cache key
Revalidate on demand with tags and paths
Keep personal data out of the shared cache
Stale page or data leak? Diagnose the cache boundary
The page that never updates: a missing revalidation
